name: Mose Adler
role: Keeper of the Saltmouth water tower
bio: Third-generation keeper of Saltmouth's condenser tower, a job he describes as 'counting cups until the desert learns manners.' He took the cracked coil the courier brought in the heat-window run and had the tower whistling by dusk — and he has forgiven the courier for the laundry line except on days ending in ritual. Blesses every pump stroke, audits every bucket, and keeps the tower's guest ledger in a hand so slow and beautiful the Guild once tried to trademark it.
appearance: A barrel-built man in his fifties with a sun-cured bald head he polishes 'so the tower sees a clean reflection and works harder,' thick expressive eyebrows, a teal-stained canvas apron heavy with brass wrenches, a brass measuring cup on a cord around his neck (the official cup, capacity disputed), and sandals resoled with old tyre tread. Perpetually damp left cuff from blessing procedures.
voice: Slow, grateful, faintly tyrannical about cups. Speaks in measurements and blessings: everything is cups, buckets, tower-feet. Says 'counted twice' as both hello and farewell. Never raises his voice; raises his eyebrows, which is worse. Calls the tower 'she' and the Guild 'the weather with a ledger.' His gratitude is enormous and slightly burdensome, like being hugged by a water main.

greetings: Courier. The cups are counted, the pumps are blessed, and you are — let me check the ledger — welcome. Twice.
Ash Varga. The coil still holds. I tell her good morning every day and I mention your name, which she deserves.
Come in out of the wind. Water's free. The cup is not optional. The cup is the water's handshake.
barks: Someone took a bucket without signing. I'm not angry. I'm updating the liturgy.
She condensed forty-one cups last night. Forty-one! In this air! That's not engineering, that's devotion.
The Guild offered to meter the tower. I offered to meter their heads. We are negotiating.
That laundry line has been there thirty years. It has seniority. You drift under it or you answer to my wife, and she irons angry.
mission: That coil you brought — cracked, scorned, Guild-certified 'serviceable' — she runs on it like a hymn. If you pass the exchange, tell the factor her paperwork holds pressure worse than her parts.
East gate cistern reads low. If your route bends that way, read the gauge to me on the radio. Numbers first, opinions after, that's the tower way.
radio: Tower to Varga. Slow at the mast corner, child, the line's full of sheets and they have no brakes.
Mose here. Condensation's up a cup and a half. Whatever you did out there today, the air liked it.
Radio check from the tower. Reading you at full cups. That means five-by-five. I keep a translation chart and it makes the Guild furious. Counted twice, out.
cups: One cup per visitor. Two if you carried something heavy. Three if what you carried was bad news and you carried it anyway.
People say 'just a cup of water' like a cup is small. A cup is the entire desert, poured carefully.
The brass cup is official. The chipped enamel cup is for friends. The trough is for goats and, once, a Guild auditor. The trough was honoured.
storm: Wall's coming. She knows — pressure dips before the bell rings. Two hundred years of towers and they all learned weather before people did.
Storm rule at my tower: straps checked, cistern capped, cups counted. The sand gets in everything else, it doesn't get in the count.
night: Night condensation is the best condensation. Cool air, quiet pumps. She whispers and I write it down.
The mast reads like a slow newspaper after dark, Bahro says. My tower reads like a bank statement. Both accurate. Mine has better news.
farewells: Flat salt, courier. The ledger says you drank once and thanked twice. Correct ratio. Come back.
Go careful past the line. Not the laundry's sake — yours. Sheets are undefeated. Counted twice.
